excerpt: Hitik #2 sitao is a pole sitao variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2020 as NSIC 2020 Ps 07. BPI Lbncrdpsc bred it. It takes about 46 days from sowing to the first harvest, with 13.62 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Hitik #2 sitao takes about 46 days from sowing to the first harvest. That is about the average of the 7 pole sitao varieties with a day count, 45.4 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 13.62 t/ha beats the average of its group, 11.33. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer).

The pests and diseases that hit sitao fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its pods grew about 52.69 cm long. The seed coat is glossy black.
Where and when to plant Hitik #2 sitao

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Pole sitao climbs a trellis and bears for weeks, while bush sitao needs no trellis and comes in at once. Pick long, dark green pods that snap cleanly, and a variety rated against the bean fly and rust if you can. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).
